our_title: SCOTCH_graphTabLoad() reads mapping files with fscanf: out-of-range numbers silently wrap
ran:
repro/COR-15-twins/tabload.c on m4x4.grf (from git show v7.0.18): pristine 32-bit mapping '1
0 4294967298' -> 'SCOTCH_graphTabLoad ret=0 parttab[0]=2'; count '4294967297' -> ret=0 (read as 1); label '4294967296' -> ret=0 (label 0); pristine 64-bit '0 18446744073709551618' -> parttab[0]=9223372036854775807 (saturated). Patched (commit 0006): 'ERROR: intLoad: overflow' / 'SCOTCH_graphTabLoad: bad input (1|2)', ret=1, parttab untouched (-1), 32 and 64 bit; valid file '2
1 3
0 2' -> ret=0 parttab {2,3}. check_prog_gmap, check_prog_gpart_overlap, check_prog_gpart_remap, check_scotch_graph_part_ovl pass on 32/64-bit trees.
evidence: library_graph_map_io.c:99 'if ((fscanf (stream, GNUMSTRING, &mappfileval) != 1) || /* Read number of mapping pairs */' and :120 'if (fscanf (stream, GNUMSTRING GNUMSTRING,' -- C leaves fscanf %d overflow undefined; glibc wraps (int) or saturates (long).

fix_options.label: A. Read the numbers with intLoad() like every other Scotch loader (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Replace the two fscanf calls by intLoad(), which rejects out-of-range values since ff9d5a54.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Same accepted syntax (whitespace, optional sign, decimal digits).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: One-line idiom swap; library_graph_map_io.c already includes common.h.

fix_options.label: B. Leave fscanf and document the limit
